items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: my cousin, we called Bunch, Ivy, she got a bass fiddle and started playing it.

ctx.x: Yeah. Ivy, Verne and Vonne. And after Floyd Ray had broken up, as I say, I guess around '45 or something, then my cousin, we called Bunch, Ivy, she got a bass fiddle and started playing it. And they formed a little trio. One of them played the drums, or guitar, or something, and one played the piano, and Bunch played the bass. And they
were very successful. They made a couple of movies, you know, played the bits in a couple of movies, like that.

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: She came to Kansas City and visited me when they were passing through.

ctx.x: Now, what did she do, this Ivy?

Ivy, she played piano and sang. And she -- shortly after I left Texas, she had joined a trio, and they sang at the capital for the legislators, and so forth. And they became pretty prominent. And then she moved to California, and she sang with Floyd Ray and his band. She came to Kansas City and visited me when they were passing through.
Now, was she part of that trio that sang with Floyd Ray?
